No, that is not true. The Swiss permit system is not the same as the EU permit system. In Switzerland, residence permits are governed by the Foreign Nationals and Integration Act (Ausländer- und Integrationsgesetz, AIG). The type of permit a foreign national receives depends on various factors, including their purpose of stay (e.g., work, study, family reunification), their country of origin, and the specific cantonal and federal regulations.

There is no automatic "C permit" (C-Bewilligung) granted after five years for all EU citizens regardless of their country of origin. The C permit is a permanent residence permit, but its issuance depends on meeting specific criteria related to integration, financial independence, and compliance with Swiss law. EU citizens may have different rights under bilateral agreements, but the process is not automatic after a fixed period for everyone.
